summary.headline: The Southborough Youth Commission voted to allocate up to $5,000 from its donation account for furniture ahead of moving to Flagg School.
summary.summary: The Southborough Youth Commission met on March 10, 2026, to review department programs and approve funding for its upcoming office move. The commission voted unanimously to spend up to $5,000 from its revolving donation account on fire-retardant furnishings for its planned relocation to Flagg School by July 1. Members also analyzed declining utilization data for the town's $15,000 INTERFACE mental health referral service contract, concluding the service should remain unchanged while staff increases outreach. In addition, the board discussed school programming, camp scholarship applications, and upcoming spring community events.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The commission opened the meeting, approved the minutes from the previous month, and adjourned at the end of the evening.
key_details: Meeting called to order at 7:05 p.m.
Approved minutes from the February 10, 2026 meeting.
Adjourned at 8:15 p.m.
topics.outcome: Meeting opened, minutes approved, and meeting adjourned.

topics.title: Spring meeting schedule and scholarship reviews
topics.summary: The commission reviewed upcoming meeting dates for April and May. The board agreed to hold its April meeting in person to review applications for community awards, while the regular May date will be rescheduled because it conflicts with local elections.
key_details: The April meeting will be held in person to facilitate selection for awards.
The board will judge the Laurie Sugarman-Whittier Wellness Award and the Ellen Piantek Scholarship at the April meeting.
The May meeting originally fell on town election night and will be rescheduled by staff.
topics.outcome: Staff will poll members to reschedule the May meeting date.

topics.title: Director's report on department operations and programs
topics.summary: The director provided an update on staffing, school initiatives, and community assistance programs. The department hired an intern from Boston University for the upcoming academic year and received cultural arts funding to continue senior housing art sessions. Updates were also provided on camp scholarships and mental health outreach in regional schools.
key_details: Boston University graduate intern Cooper Harris will join the department from fall 2026 through spring 2027.
A grant was received from the Southborough Cultural Arts Council to maintain the Crafty Crew program at Colonial Gardens.
Staff provided relationship safety programming and screen-unplugging workshops to students at Algonquin Regional High School.
Approximately 10 families have submitted camp scholarship requests to date, supported by a $10,000 Friends budget.
Food pantry outreach by department staff is transitioning from bi-monthly to monthly.
topics.outcome: Informational update; no formal action required.

topics.title: Flagg School relocation furniture funding
topics.summary: The commission discussed furnishing requirements for the department's pending move to Flagg School, expected no later than July 1. Because municipal rules require certified fire-retardant upholstery and the new office layout cannot accommodate certain existing desks, the commission voted to spend up to $5,000 from its revolving donation fund to purchase replacements.
key_details: Offices are relocating to Flagg School, with an expected move date no later than July 1, 2026.
Existing upholstered chairs cannot be moved because new town spaces require fire-retardant materials.
The department revolving donation account had an uncommitted balance of $6,029.56.
Usable furniture that cannot be transferred may be donated to charitable groups such as Fresh Start Furniture Bank.
The board approved an expenditure cap of $5,000 for desks and compliant seating.
topics.outcome: Approved spending up to $5,000 from the donation account by unanimous roll-call vote.
topics.why_it_matters: Authorizes town donation funds to furnish municipal youth and family services offices relocating to Flagg School.

topics.title: INTERFACE mental health referral service utilization review
topics.summary: The director presented utilization figures for the town's contract with the William James College INTERFACE Referral Service. Between July 1 and December 31, 2025, Southborough residents utilized the service for only 8 cases, consistent with regional declines across neighboring communities. Commissioners weighed whether to keep the current $15,000 unlimited contract or adopt a restricted gatekeeper model, deciding to keep the existing contract while monitoring trends and improving public awareness.
key_details: The town pays $15,000 annually for an unlimited community subscription to INTERFACE.
Only 8 case referrals were logged from July 1 through December 31, 2025, compared to past highs of 43 cases.
Regional directors confirmed similar usage declines across other MetroWest communities.
Alternative resources, including state call lines and community behavioral health urgent care centers, may explain reduced local usage.
The commission reached consensus to maintain the contract structure for the coming year and promote the service more actively.
topics.outcome: Consensus reached to maintain the current contract model and increase publicity; staff will discuss contract details with INTERFACE representatives.

topics.title: Friends of Youth Commission update
topics.summary: A representative reported on behalf of the Friends of the Southborough Youth Commission regarding an upcoming community event and fundraising needs. The Friends will co-host an open house on March 27, 2026, at Theracopia to increase awareness of department services and recruit new volunteers.
key_details: The Nurture and Network open house is scheduled for March 27, 2026, from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. at Theracopia.
The event includes donated wellness stations, acupuncture demonstrations, and raffle prizes.
The Friends organization is seeking new members to assist with low-labor fundraising and department support.

votes.motion: Approve spending up to $5,000 from the donation account for furniture-related expenses for the Department of Youth and Family Services.
